SUMMARY

Resolution Nos. 7581, 7582, and 7583 establish terms of employment and compensation
for City employees represented by the Arcadia Police Civilian Employees’ Association
(“APCEA”), the Arcadia Police Officers’ Association (“APOA”), and the Arcadia Public
Works Employees’ Association (“APWEA”). Pursuant to the Meyers-Milias-Brown Act, the
City met and conferred in good faith concerning wages, benefits, and other terms and
conditions of employment.

Staff report attachments are subject to the results of the City Council Closed Session on
July 2, 2024. It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution Nos. 7581, 7582,
and 7583 establishing compensation and related benefits for employees represented by
the APCEA, APOA, and APWEA for July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2027.

BACKGROUND

The APCEA, APOA, and APWEA are recognized employee organizations with a total of
130 budgeted positions:

  •  APCEA includes 21 budgeted positions that play an integral role in the operations
  of the Police Department, including emergency dispatch services, police records,
  logistics, and maintaining and processing criminal evidence.

  •  APOA includes 63 budgeted Police Officers and Police Sergeants that play a vital
  role in protecting life and property, provide professional police services, and work
  in partnership with the community.

  •  APWEA includes 46 budgeted positions that provide essential services to the
  community, such as the utility’s maintenance of infrastructure that provides reliable
  water to residents and businesses of Arcadia, maintenance and repair of streets,
  including emergency repairs, as well as services for sewer, solid waste, street
  sweeping, and maintenance of City buildings and fleet.

The previous APCEA, APOA, and APWEA Memorandums of Understanding (“MOU”)
were in effect from July 1, 2021, through June 30, 2024. Negotiations with the APCEA
and APOA began in February 2024, while negotiations with APWEA began in April 2024.
During the course of negotiations, the City’s negotiating team and the groups’ negotiating
teams held a combined total of 23 meetings in an attempt to reach a tentative agreement
that would be beneficial to both the City and the bargaining groups.

DISCUSSION

The City continuously analyzes and takes steps to meet current and future challenges,
including continually shifting economic factors, retirement costs, and a rapidly changing

labor market. A Total Compensation Study was conducted to help inform the City’s
position in overall compensation, relative to the marketplace. Although compensation
pieces varied, the City’s contribution toward health insurance was behind the market
across each group.
Discussions during negotiations centered around the ability to provide competitive, fair-
market salaries and how to most effectively address unprecedented recruitment and
retention challenges while maintaining long-term fiscal stability.

Throughout negotiations, the parties met and conferred in good faith and ultimately
reached a tentative agreement for the period of July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2027.
Each MOU contains package modifications that address:

  •  Salary and other compensation
  •  Health Insurance
  •  Leave Banks and Service Credit
  •  MOU Clean-up Language to comply with State law
  •  Miscellaneous items specific to each Association

Resolution Nos. 7581, 7582, and 7583, will aid the City’s efforts to recruit and retain well-
qualified staff to continue to provide high quality services to the community. Agenda item
attachments, which include Resolution Nos. 7581, 7582, 7583 and the applicable exhibits
for each, are subject to the results of the City Council Closed Session on July 2, 2024.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

The proposed action does not constitute a project under the California Environmental
Quality Act (“CEQA”), based on Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines, as it can
be seen with certainty that it will have no impact on the environment.

FISCAL IMPACT

Fiscal impact will be discussed after conclusion of the Closed Session discussion on July
2, 2024. A supplemental budget appropriation will be brought forward at the next City
Council meeting, if needed.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council determine that this action does not constitute a
project under the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”), and adopt the following
Resolutions:

  Resolution No. 7581 approving a Memorandum of Understanding establishing
  compensation and related benefits for employees represented by the Arcadia
